title: Bound the shared zod tool-argument primitives in src/tools/args.ts
description: In the gitignored checkout applications/mcp-gateway/repos/mongodb-mcp-server (branch main, pre-fix pinned commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0), tighten the shared zod primitives in src/tools/args.ts: give CommonArgs.string() (lines 22-23) a maxLength alongside its no-Unicode regex; add a safe character pattern to AtlasArgs.password() (lines 74-76, keep min 1 / max 100); replace zEJSON() (lines 86-90, currently z.object({}).loose().transform(toEJSON)) with a bounded z.record of length-capped string keys whose values validate as EJSON, cap value size and nesting depth, and reject unknown $-prefixed MongoDB operators against an allowlist. Do not change exported signatures. Constraints: the vitest unit-tests CI gate is blocking and must stay green; semgrep SAST is advisory; no deployment windows or change freeze are configured in sdlc/policy.json, so scheduling follows the releaseProcess environmentsOrder dev -> qa -> prod with one approval and a documented rollback.
acceptanceCriteria: grep for z.object({}).loose in src/tools/args.ts returns nothing; zEJSON() is a bounded z.record with length-capped keys and a MongoDB operator allowlist
CommonArgs.string() enforces a maxLength and AtlasArgs.password() enforces a pattern as well as min 1 / max 100

A new vitest case shows a 10,000-character string value and a document with an unknown $-prefixed operator key are both rejected by the schema before toEJSON or driver invocation, and the vitest run exits 0

verificationMethod.description: Reviewer inspects the src/tools/args.ts diff and the vitest output on the PR: expected result - zEJSON, CommonArgs.string and AtlasArgs.password each enforce length, pattern and operator bounds and the suite passes.

rootCause.description: The shared zod primitives in src/tools/args.ts were written for developer convenience without security bounds: zEJSON is an open z.object({}).loose() record and CommonArgs.string has a regex but no maxLength, so no length or operator constraint reaches database-bound arguments.
